Issued at 1127 AM CDT Tue Oct 6 2026

A northwesterly flow continues across the Plains as an upper 
level ridge remains in place across the western United States. 
An upper level trough was embedded in this northwest flow and 
was crossing the Northern Plains. At the surface a trough of low
pressure and warm wedge of 850mb temperatures extended from 
southwest Nebraska into eastern Colorado. Models remain in good
agreement with the surface trough crossing southwest Kansas 
late tonight as the northern plains upper trough moves into the 
upper Mississippi Valley. This boundary will then stall out 
just south of the Oklahoma border on Wednesday and then lift 
north towards Nebraska late week. 850mb temperatures cool by 
2-4C as this boundary passes tonight but these temperatures are
still 60-70% greater than climatology for this time of year. 
As a result the current NBM guidance with highs mainly in the 
mid 80s still look on track Wednesday afternoon. These 850mb 
temperatures are then forecast not change much through the 
remainder of the week and into the weekend period 

Warm and dry conditions can be expected through the weekend. 
Models today remain in good agreement in keeping a northwest 
flow across the Plains through the upcoming weekend with 850mb 
temperatures each afternoon ranging mainly from 18 to around 
22c. Based on this and the run to run agreement with the models 
with this solution, it looks like southwest Kansas can look 
forward to temperatures staying slightly above the seasonal 
normal for this time of year through the weekend. Even with this
said the NBM guidance for temperatures over the past several 
days has had a cool bias so would not be surprised if a few 
locations (mainly south central Kansas) will not end up several 
degrees warmer than the current forecast this weekend. Current 
guidance for highs through the weekend is for highs to be mainly
in the mid 80s. 

Windy conditions this weekend. The upper level ridge over the 
western United States will weaken and shift east late week as 
our next, significant, upper level trough exits the eastern 
Pacific and begins to move across the Pacific Northwest. As this
next upper level trough moves into western United States and 
deepens, the surface trough of low pressure along the lee of the
Rockies deepen. This will result in a tightening surface 
pressure to develop across western Kansas. In addition a 40 knot
low level jet forecast by the ensembles mean also support a 
period of windy conditions as these stronger winds mix down to 
the surface. Current ensemble and NBM max wind gusts forecast 
for the weekend appears to be on track with gusts in excess of 
40 mph being possible at times Saturday and Sunday afternoon. A 
few areas could even see wind gusts as high at 50 mph if a few 
of the models verify that far out. 

Looking ahead to next week, we still are monitoring the chances
for precipitation early in the week along with some cooler 
temperatures as the deepening upper level trough over the 
western United States over the weekend begins to move 
east/northeast and weaken. Models still differ on timing/track 
of this next upper wave next week but when compared to what the 
models were forecasting next week 24 hours earlier it does 
appear that the models are beginning to converge on a slower 
solution with the upper trough crossing the Plains now mid week.
Based on this there still appears to be improving chances for 
precipitation ahead of this system early in the week as this 
upper trough approaches and the our next cold front drops south 
into southwest Kansas. The best opportunity for rain and cooler 
temperatures now however appears to be around the middle of the 
next week. As for temperatures following the cold front...there 
will be a period of unseasonably cool temperatures following 
this cold front, especially if we have cloud/precipitation 
during the day. Current probability for highs from Tuesday 
through Thursday to be less than 70s degrees ranges from 40 to 
50 percent north and west of Dodge City. In the same area the 
probability for lows during the same time frame to be less than 
45 degrees ranges from 20-30%.
